messages.subject: annotation_legend ?
parts:
Hi,

Skimming through the latticeExtra webpage, I found this idea (among
others) quite interesting to share:

http://latticeextra.r-forge.r-project.org/#panel.key&theme=theEconomist

Squeezing the legend inside the plot panel is something that's often
needed for journals with tight length limits. Having a convenient
interface to specify the position of the legend inside a panel would
be quite useful. Currently, opts(legend.position) is given in
normalised units relative to the full ggplot viewport, which requires
trial and error in my experience (and ggplot2 can be slow..)

If the legend grob can be extracted, or perhaps even only a part of it
(e.g. only linetype goes to one panel), some variation of
annotation_custom() could be used to place it inside one panel, with a
position given as data coordinates (including Inf for convenience),
and the standard justification hjust,vjust.


Best,

baptiste

messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: Re: annotation_legend ?
parts:
Facets are indeed a tricky question. One could wish to specify,

- the nrow+ncol that identifies the facet(s). Default to all, or first
one only perhaps.

- the condition, derived from the data, that selects the correct facet(s)

- to plot in empty panels, e.g. when using facet_wrap with odd number
of panels (in which case, a more suitable coordinate system might be
more like ?legend in base graphics, i.e "top", "topright", ...

My personal preference would be to allow all the above, for maximum convenience.

Once this decision is made, the actual implementation is probably
quite similar to annotation_custom.

Best,

b.

> Facets are indeed a tricky question. One could wish to specify,
>
> - the nrow+ncol that identifies the facet(s). Default to all, or first
> one only perhaps.
>
> - the condition, derived from the data, that selects the correct facet(s)
This is generally what I prefer, but for legends maybe numeric position is ok.

> - to plot in empty panels, e.g. when using facet_wrap with odd number
> of panels (in which case, a more suitable coordinate system might be
> more like ?legend in base graphics, i.e "top", "topright", ...
It should be easy to discover empty space by inspecting the gtable.

> My personal preference would be to allow all the above, for maximum convenience.
>
> Once this decision is made, the actual implementation is probably
> quite similar to annotation_custom.

Except that legends don't exist independently in that way. My feeling
would be that it would be easiest to implement during the placement of
the legend grob.

On 12 January 2012 09:32, Hadley Wickham <had...@rice.edu> wrote:
> On Wed, Jan 11, 2012 at 1:27 PM, baptiste auguie
> <baptist...@googlemail.com> wrote:
>> Facets are indeed a tricky question. One could wish to specify,
>>
>> - the nrow+ncol that identifies the facet(s). Default to all, or first
>> one only perhaps.
>>
>> - the condition, derived from the data, that selects the correct facet(s)
>
> This is generally what I prefer, but for legends maybe numeric position is ok.
>
>> - to plot in empty panels, e.g. when using facet_wrap with odd number
>> of panels (in which case, a more suitable coordinate system might be
>> more like ?legend in base graphics, i.e "top", "topright", ...
>
> It should be easy to discover empty space by inspecting the gtable.
>
>> My personal preference would be to allow all the above, for maximum convenience.
>>
>> Once this decision is made, the actual implementation is probably
>> quite similar to annotation_custom.
>
> Except that legends don't exist independently in that way.  My feeling
> would be that it would be easiest to implement during the placement of
> the legend grob.

Quite possibly, yes. However, the idea of making it an annotation
instead is that ggplot2, in its logic, would always by default use an
external location for the legend (which always works, for all plots),
but for the final cosmetic tweaks before publication one could
disassemble the plot and place the legend in a very plot-specific
position. In this regard, having it as an annotation also gives more
freedom to modify the grob with grid before placing it, or even use a
different grob altogether (a feature that should probably not be
implemented in the pure grammar of graphics framework where the legend
should be purely automated, but could be useful as a kind of
post-processing -- an annotation).

Just my 2c (and they're not worth much in NZ $ ;)

Cheers,

b.
